Tariff-refund funding running out and the Sam's bundle are the counterweights.

evidence.text: BJ's direct competitor Sam's Club reported the SAME Aug-Oct quarter on 2026-11-19: US comp ex fuel +4.9% (Q2: +4.4%), transactions +5.1%. Costco's US comp ex gas ran 5.6% (Aug), 8.0% (Sep) and 8.1% (Oct), about 7.3% for BJ's quarter against 7.2% in Costco's May-Aug Q4, when BJ printed 3.1%. The club channel was stable to accelerating, against a street bar for BJ of 2.5% (BofA) to 3% (Zacks) and an easy 1.8% compare from last year's Q3.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: BJ trades on comp ex gas. Q1 FY26 comp 1.5% gave -8.25%. Q2 FY26 comp 3.1% plus a raise gave +5.61%. Q3 FY25 comp 1.8% with an EPS beat gave +1.13% (baseline; company 8-Ks).
evidence.why_not_priced: Sam's printed this morning, the day before BJ, and street comp estimates (2.5-3%) were set before it and sit below BJ's own Q2 rate. If priced, previews would quote a comp above 3%. They quote 2.5-3%.
evidence.independence: Costco October sales release, a different company and document (https://www.morningstar.com/news/globe-newswire/9870370/costco-wholesale-corporation-reports-october-sales-results, 2026-11-04; August: https://www.rttnews.com/3688055/costco-net-sales-comps-rise-in-august-q4.aspx). evidence.link: Same channel and format: Sam's and Costco are the two other US membership warehouse clubs, overlapping BJ's East Coast/Southeast/Texas footprint. Sam's numbers cover the identical Aug-Oct quarter (Walmart Q3 ended 2026-10-31; BJ Q3 ended ~2026-11-01).

evidence.text: Gasoline over BJ's Q3 was mostly a rising-price quarter: the AAA national average went from ~$4.10 in early Sept to a record $4.48 on 2026-09-24 (crude ~$100, Strait of Hormuz), then eased only to $4.22 by 2026-10-29. Murphy USA's Jul-Sep retail fuel margin was 27.4 cpg against 28.3 a year earlier, and same-store gallons were +0.1%. BJ's Q2 fuel outperformance came from a 'pullback from peak gas prices', so Q3 fuel profit per gallon is likely below Q2's outsized level and the EPS beat likely smaller than Q2's 16%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gas profit drove the Q2 FY26 beat and raise, and the stock went +5.61%. No other quarter's fuel line has been isolated.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced. TIKR and others already expect fuel to 'normalize', and EPS consensus is +6-9% y/y, not the +19% of Q2. If fully priced, the whisper would sit at or below consensus. It sits 4 cents above, so some of the Q2 fuel windfall is still expected.
evidence.independence: AAA weekly releases (https://gasprices.aaa.com/national-average-dips-following-record-setting-september/, 2026-10-01; https://gasprices.aaa.com/news/page/3?lv=true). Murphy's 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001573516/000157351626000193/exh991_09302026er.htm. Macro-to-company transmission, not confirmed by BJ.
evidence.link: Murphy USA is a high-volume, price-led US fuel retailer, the same business as BJ's gas stations. The retail fuel margin is the line BJ credited for the Q2 beat and raise. No shared customer or revenue figure.

evidence.text: Retail gasoline has fallen fast since BJ's quarter closed: AAA $4.22 (2026-10-29), $4.10 (11-05), $3.90 (11-12), $3.72 (11-19), as crude fell from >$100 to the high $80s and lower. Pump prices falling behind wholesale is the setup in which retail fuel margins widen. That gives a Q4 fuel-profit tailwind in the line management credited for the August raise, and supports a FY EPS guide above $4.60-4.80. Q4 needs only ~$1.00-1.06 against $0.96 last year.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 FY26 FY EPS raise on gas outperformance got +5.61%. Q3 FY25 (2025-11-21) also raised the FY outlook, with an EPS beat and a soft comp, and got +1.13%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The street FY (~$4.70) sits at the guide midpoint, so no Q4 fuel windfall is in it. If priced, FY estimates would have moved above $4.80 in November. Zacks shows only +1 cent in 7 days and Investing.com +1.6% in 60 days.
evidence.independence: Mechanism from the BLS note on rising/falling margins (https://www.bls.gov/opub/btn/volume-4/as-crude-oil-plunges-retail-gasoline-margins-spike-then-retreat.htm). Company basis: the 8-K of 2026-08-21 credits gas for the raise. Proxy: BJ has not confirmed Q4 fuel margins.

evidence.text: Merchandise margin funding thins in Q3. Management said the tariff refunds that funded H1 price cuts are 'nearly exhausted' going into the back half; Q2 merch margin was already -20bp y/y with the refunds. In Q3 BJ ran a 42%-off anniversary event (2026-09-24 to 10-31) across dozens of items. Replacement funding (supplier money, retail media, gas) is unproven, and Earnings Whispers frames -10 to -20bp as fine and worse as traffic bought at rising cost.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 FY25 merch margin -50bp (8-K 2026-03-05) got -1.51%. Q2 FY26 merch margin -20bp, offset by fuel, got +5.61%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: previews flag it, but nobody quantifies the merch margin, and the EPS consensus rising into the print suggests no margin step-down is modelled. If priced, Q3 EPS estimates would have been cut since August. They rose 1.6%.
evidence.independence: Promo: BJ's Business Wire 2026-09-22 (https://secure.businesswire.com/news/home/20260922406849/en/BJs-Wholesale-Club-Celebrates-42-Years-of-Delivering-Unbeatable-Value-By-Delivering-Even-More-Value). evidence.why_not_priced: The gain was disclosed in August and consensus Q3 EPS growth of 6-9% is well below Q2's 19%, so this is largely in the bar. It matters only if the Q3 beat is read against Q2's quality.

Management said on 2026-11-19 it drew 'a couple million new members' in its first month, and Sam's is investing in fresh-food price. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: BJ's membership fee hike (2024) was bought. No prior reaction to a competitor's membership pricing is on record here.
evidence.why_not_priced: Uptake numbers became public only this morning. BJ's previews discuss MFI slowing from lapping its own fee hike, not a competitor bundle. If priced, previews would mention the bundle. None found does.

evidence.link: Direct substitute: a Sam's Club Plus membership competes for the same warehouse-club member. BJ's Club+ fee is also $120. No overlap figure is available.

evidence.text: Q2's gross-margin help from tariff refunds does not recur. Merchandise margin was +110bp in Q2, of which 65bp came from tariff refunds; management said 'all of the refunds that we expect to receive were received' and 'most of it has been recognized', with only a small residual in Q3. Q3 gross margin therefore has to beat last year's 48.0% without that 65bp. Consensus EBIT of $56.05m (-8.5% y/y) already assumes contraction.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gross margin is the line this name trades on. Q1 gross margin -50bp: -9.13%. Q2 gross margin +40bp, flattered by the refund, with an EPS beat: +2.74%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced. UBS and the iTiger preview both expect gross-margin contraction, and consensus EPS is -8.85% y/y. What may not be fully priced is that the comparison is against a refund-flattered Q2: if the street extrapolated Q2's +40bp, the Q3 gross-margin print reads worse than trend.
evidence.independence: The UBS view of Q3 gross-margin contraction (https://www.itiger.com/news/1134066982) is a different source pointing the same way.

evidence.text: Operating cost deleverage on weaker comps. In Q2, comps of +2.1% still produced +140bp of SG&A deleverage (marketing +45bp, store labor +35bp, health insurance +30bp, supplies +20bp) and +70bp of buying, distribution and occupancy deleverage. Q3 comps were only +0.6% on 451 stores vs 442 a year earlier. Applying Q2's ~9.6% SG&A dollar growth to Q3 gives SG&A of about 31.0% of sales. With flat-to-down gross margin that is EBIT of about $55m vs $56.05m consensus and EPS of about $0.86 vs $0.88.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's operating-margin decline of -100bp was overlooked on an EPS beat (+2.74%). Q1's margin pressure was sold (-9.13%).
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus already embeds an EBIT decline of about 8.5%. My estimate is only about $1m of EBIT below it, inside the noise of a disputed bar. If it were fully priced, consensus would sit at about $0.86, not $0.88-0.92.
evidence.independence: The SG&A breakdown comes from the Q2 call (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/BKE/Q22026), which shares a quarter with the release. Store count (451 vs 442) is from the 2026-11-05 sales release. Both rest on the Q2 reporting, so they count once.

evidence.text: Comps decelerated through Q3 in the company's own monthly releases: August +1.6% (net sales +3.6%), September +0.5% (+2.2%), October -0.5% (+1.8%). These are against tough prior-year compares (September 2025 comps were +6.9%). evidence.text: Q3 2026 is mostly pre-booked and should land near consensus. At the 2026-08-28 Q2 release, Q3 VLCC days were 86% booked at $156,900/day, Suezmax 79% at $117,400 and LR2/Aframax 70% at $81,000, with management saying the full quarter would come in below those levels on ballast days. Against Q2 actuals ($152.7k/$111.5k/$92.4k) and two VLCCs sold in Aug/Sep, that points to an adjusted EPS of about $2.3-2.5 against the $2.27-2.29 consensus. The small upside is the 14-30% of open days fixed during the late-September spike: DHT's Q3 VLCC spot was $167.1k, and peers DHT and Okeanis beat Q3 consensus by 15% and 108%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 missed consensus ($2.61 against $2.74) and the stock rose about +0.5% to +1%. Q3 2025 missed by $0.05 and fell 6.7% over the week. On this line the stock reacts muted and mixed.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the bookings have been public since August and consensus sits right on them. The only unpriced part is the late-September fixing on open days. If that were priced, consensus would sit above $2.5, as it did not after the DHT/Okeanis beats.
evidence.independence: DHT Q3 VLCC spot $167.1k/day and a 15% EPS beat (https://www.bairdmaritime.com/shipping/tankers/dht-holdings-third-quarter-profit). Teekay's Q3 Suezmax spot was $106.4k and LR2 $67.6k, both below FRO's bookings (https://www.bairdmaritime.com/shipping/tankers/teekay-tankers-net-income-falls). That cuts the LR2/Suezmax upside and is why the size is small.

evidence.text: FRO's Q4-to-date bookings, published in this release, will be a record far above Q3, going by same-quarter peers reported 9-11 Nov. DHT booked 68% of Q4 VLCC spot days at $579,900/day (9 Nov). Okeanis booked 48% of VLCC spot days at $688,800 and 60% of Suezmax days at $410,900 (11 Nov). Teekay booked Q4 Suezmax at $272,000 and Aframax/LR2 at $208,300 (11 Nov). FRO's Q3 levels were $157k/$117k/$81k. On FRO's fleet (40 VLCC, 19 Suezmax, 18 LR2) that implies a Q4 EPS several times the about $2.5 Q4 the stale FY consensus ($9.02) leaves room for. The peers' stocks did not move on the same disclosure: DHT was flat to +1.8%, Okeanis -0.3%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: FRO gives quarter-to-date bookings every print. Q2 2026's Q3 bookings ($157k against Q2 bookings of $181.7k) came with a +0.5-1% move. Peers this month: DHT about flat to +1.8% on $579.9k, Okeanis -0.3% on $688.8k. The market does not pay much for record forward bookings at a perceived peak.
evidence.why_not_priced: The level is largely telegraphed by peers. What is not is FRO's own mix: its Q3 VLCC rate ($157k) trailed Okeanis ($269k) and DHT ($167k), so FRO's Gulf exposure and Q4 rate are unknown. Street FY numbers do not reflect it either ($9.02 on 1 Nov implies a Q4 near Q3). If it were priced, FY consensus would be $13+ and the stock would not sit 22% below its November high.
evidence.independence: Okeanis: https://finviz.com/news/421910/okeanis-eco-tankers-doubles-consensus-and-locks-in-a-huge-q4-but-the-rate-peak-may-already-be-behind-it (2026-11-12). Teekay: https://www.bairdmaritime.com/shipping/tankers/teekay-tankers-net-income-falls (2026-11-11). Three different companies, so three independent documents, but one read-through.
evidence.link: same spot markets in the same quarter: DHT and Okeanis trade VLCCs (FRO 40 VLCCs), Okeanis and Teekay trade Suezmax (FRO 19), Teekay trades Aframax/LR2 (FRO 18)

evidence.text: The spot market corrected sharply after FRO last spoke. Gulf of Oman-China VLCC fell to about WS308 on 13 Nov, 64% below the WS841 record of 8 Oct (Reuters via gCaptain, 16 Nov). TD22 (US Gulf-China) was down 63.6% and TD3C earnings down 25% to about $1.06m/day. Several Suezmax/Aframax routes fell 50-70% in the week to 6 Nov, and Okeanis management put VLCC spot near $350k and Suezmax at $150-200k. FRO's open Q4 days and its Q1 2027 commentary will be priced off these lower levels.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not observed on FRO's own prints. On equities, FRO is -22% in November while rates fell; Okeanis's cautious remarks on its print came with -0.3%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the stock fell 22% month to date. What is not priced is how cautiously management frames Q1 2027 on the call. If that were fully in, the stock would have stabilised and the skew would be flatter than +21.6.
evidence.independence: https://cyprusshippingnews.com/2026/11/12/atlantic-tanker-earnings-fall-faster-than-gulf-earnings/ (Baltic via Signal Ocean, week to 6 Nov: TD22 -16.2% w/w, -34.9% from peak; Aframax TD19 -69.8%).

evidence.why_not_priced: The drawdown is driven by rates and Hormuz headlines, not by FRO-specific numbers. The positive skew says the market still pays for more downside, so this is a lean that cuts against the option market and is sized small. If the setup were priced as a relief candidate, puts would not be bid at +21.6.

evidence.text: Hormuz headline risk sits inside the one-day window. On 17 Nov Iran's foreign minister visited Oman to discuss maritime corridors, and Oman said it hoped a temporary Hormuz shipping corridor could be announced soon. The US-Iran track is stalled and attacks on tankers have increased. An announcement would hit tanker equities regardless of the print: tanker shares fell on earlier reopening headlines, DHT -3% on Iran's reopening offer.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: DHT about -3% on Iran's offer to reopen the strait (Motley Fool/Nasdaq). Lloyd's List reported FRO -2% on a Hormuz-traffic day.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is a tail inside the window, partly in the put skew. The expected value is small, and a lean against the print happens only if the announcement lands on 20 Nov.
evidence.independence: https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/why-dht-holdings-stock-dropped-today (DHT down on a reopening offer). This is a proxy: macro to company.

evidence.text: FRO has less Q4 spot leverage than its pure-spot peers. Barstad said VLCC revenue cover was 'slightly above 30%' (policy: about a third). Two newbuild VLCCs are on one-year charters at $120k/day, and two 2016 VLCCs on two- and three-year charters at $90k and $75k/day from August 2026. He conceded FRO fixed 'a little bit too early.' Fleet-wide Q4 earnings will trail what a $580k-$690k peer VLCC spot booking implies per ship.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior reaction to cover levels observed.
evidence.why_not_priced: It was disclosed in August, so the level is known. What is not settled is whether analysts mechanically apply peer spot rates to FRO's whole fleet.
evidence.independence: The charter rates and dates are in the Q2 release: https://www.financialcontent.com/article/gnwcq-2026-8-28-fro-second-quarter-and-six-months-2026-results (same company, separate document).

evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the policy is public. The finding lands inside what the company told the market to expect.

next_guide.basis: The EPS and margin guide is likely held or raised: management flagged about $35M of further benefit if the 10% Section 301 rate held through Q3, and no rate increase was found. The FY sales guide risks being trimmed to the low end: August trend supported the low end of Q3, October clothing card spend slowed to +1%, TJX blamed warm weather for a slow November, and a new Old Navy CEO started Nov 2. Net: EPS maintained or raised, sales maintained or narrowed lower.

evidence.text: GAP fell 17.2% in 20 sessions and 10.75% in 5 into the print and sits 3.35% above its 52-week low. Over the same weeks the retail sector ETF (XRT) stayed near its high, NAV $90.66 on Nov 12 against a 52-week high of 93.52. Spot about $19 is 28% below the $26.26 mean target. No company-specific cause was found for the slide. The two prints that showed an EPS beat and a margin/EPS raise paid +8.2% and +12.9%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY26 (2026-08-27): stock had drifted lower into the print, then EPS beat with a raised EPS guide and Old Navy -4%, +12.94%. Q3 FY25: +8.24% on beat and raise. Two Old Navy-driven sales-guide cuts: -14.41% and -15.40%.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is a statement about what is priced, not about what is unpriced: the bar has fallen. If the slide reflected known bad news, there would be a downgrade, a pre-release or an 8-K. None was found (EDGAR shows only Forms 3/4/144, 13D/A and a board appointment since Sep 15). Calls are bid (skew -13.2), so options partly carry this upside already. Sized below the reaction to the last beat-and-raise for that reason.
evidence.independence: Sector comparison: https://www.ssga.com/us/en/individual/etfs/state-street-spdr-sp-retail-etf-xrt. Simply Wall St 2026-11-18 also finds no single cause: https://sg.finance.yahoo.com/news/gap-gap-shares-dropped-driving-081336220.html

evidence.text: Street FY26 adjusted EPS of $2.33 sits below the company's own raised guide floor of $2.35 (range $2.35-2.45). Q3 consensus EPS of $0.73 matches only the low end of what the Q3 guide implies (sales +1.5-2.5%, GM +25-75bp on 42.4%, slight SG&A leverage on 33.9% give roughly $0.73-0.79 at ~365M shares and 25.5% tax). The street is haircutting management on EPS. The Q2 profit beat came with management saying it 'exceeded our profit expectations'.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY26 EPS beat $0.52 against $0.50 plus a raise: +12.94%. Q1 FY26 slight EPS miss plus a sales cut: -15.40%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The consensus is visible, but a street sitting under the guide floor means an in-guide print is an EPS beat. If priced, the whisper would sit above the guide midpoint rather than at $0.75. Capped small because the EPS consensus has one source.
evidence.independence: Guide arithmetic from the company 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000039911/000162828026059262/q22026eprexhibit991.htm. Same EW article as the revenue bar.

evidence.text: On the Aug 27 call the CFO said, of the Q3 sales guide of +1.5% to +2.5%, that 'our current trend supports the low end of our outlook'. On a $3.9B base the low end is about $3.96-4.00B. The street's $4.02B sits at the guide midpoint, above management's own read of trend.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue misses have coincided with large moves both ways depending on margin. Q2 FY26 revenue missed ($3.65B against $3.72B) and the stock rose 12.9% on EPS and guide. Q1 FY26 revenue miss with a sales-guide cut: -15.4%.
evidence.why_not_priced: A consensus at $4.02B, above the trend-supported low end, shows the street did not anchor on the caveat. Stock reactions on this name have followed EPS and guide more than revenue, so this is sized small.
evidence.independence: October clothing card spend slowed (BofA Institute, separate finding). Same call script as the Old Navy compare finding.

evidence.text: Old Navy laps a +6% Q3 FY25 comp, against +2% in Q2 FY25. Q2 FY26 ran -4% on a +2% compare, a two-year stack of -2. The Q3 guide of flat to -1% needs a two-year stack of +5 to +6, a 7-8 point acceleration. Old Navy is about 56% of sales ($2.06B of $3.65B in Q2). Net of the rest: Gap brand (~23%, +10% comp, lapping +7%) and BR (+3%) would have to stay strong, and Athleta (-12%) laps a weak compare.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Old Navy comp is the line the stock trades on. Misses led to -14.41% (Mar 2026) and -15.40% (May 2026). The Q2 -4% (worse than guide) was overridden by EPS and guide: +12.94%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Previews quote the flat to -1% guide and the -4% Q2 figure, but none found quotes the +6% compare. Management said in August that Q3-to-date trends were 'in line with the range'. That covers August only and lands inside the guide, which shrinks this finding.
evidence.independence: Q3 FY25 Old Navy +6% comp per Gap's Q3 FY25 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/39911/000162828025053392/q32025eprexhibit991.htm). Shares the Q2 8-K with other findings.

evidence.text: Bank of America card data (published Nov 12): clothing spend per household grew about +3.9% YoY in August, +3.6% in September and +1.0% in October, cooling more than other categories. Census October retail sales (Nov 17) also showed clothing stores declining, -0.7% m/m per a secondary report. Gap's Q3 is August to October, so the last month of its quarter was the weakest.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history of this stock reacting to card data. The line it feeds is Old Navy comp and revenue (see above).
evidence.why_not_priced: Public macro proxy: part of the pre-print slide may be this. Industry card spend averaged about +2.8% over the quarter, roughly in line with a +1.5-2.5% sales guide, so it argues for the low end rather than a miss. It is a proxy and not company-level, so it is sized small.
evidence.independence: Census October retail: https://www.wcax.com/2026/11/17/spending-growth-slowed-retail-stores-october-high-prices-give-shoppers-pause/ (clothing stores among the declines). BofA's own holiday-items cut shows clothing +8.7% in October, so the series is mixed.

evidence.text: TJX (Nov 18, same Aug-Oct quarter) posted a Marmaxx comp of +2% against about +1% expected, with apparel and home improving from Q2 (+1%). TJX rose 8-10%. It reads as an improving Q3 for value apparel. Link: TJX/Marmaxx is the largest off-price apparel competitor for the same value-apparel customer Old Navy serves, over the same August-October quarter. No revenue tie.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: GAP closed +2.5% on Nov 18, the day TJX reported.
evidence.why_not_priced: GAP already rose 2.5% on the day, so this is partly priced. Off-price gaining traffic can also be share taken from Old Navy, so the sign for Gap is ambiguous and the size small.
evidence.independence: TJX 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000109198/000010919826000058/tjxq3fy27earningspressrele.htm. Shares this document with the warm-weather finding.
evidence.link: Same product (value apparel), same customer, same quarter (TJX Q3 ended Oct 31, Gap Q3 ended ~Nov 1); competitor, not counterparty; no shared-revenue figure.

evidence.text: TJX management blamed 'unseasonably warm weather in the U.S. and Canada' for a slow start to Q4 (November) and would not say whether quarter-to-date sales were positive. The company commits to a resale registration within 30 days and a meeting within 75 days to lift authorized shares from 73.5M to 200M. The money buys advance payments for committed DC capacity and the equity portion of equipment.

evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced: -17.5% on the day and a drift to $6.59. What the print adds is the Q3 cash balance and the committed capex against it ($228M committed equipment per 247wallst). Any new raise or project-finance shortfall announced on the call would be new. If the market thought funding was settled, the stock would not have kept falling after the -17.5% day.
evidence.independence: Lind 13G: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1903145/000092963826004177/xslSCHEDULE_13G_X02/primary_doc.xml ; tickeron description of the -17% day: https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-gorilla-technology-group-grrr-stock-down-17-07-today-24274/. next_guide.basis: H1 adj EBITDA was $16.7m ($9.0m + $7.7m), so the guide needs $28.3-33.3m in H2, and H2 revenue of $86.8-91.8m (+2% to +7.5% YoY) against Q2's -5% YoY. The closest SEO-led US affiliate peer (Catena) pre-announced Q3 NA revenue -29% on AI search, and DraftKings plans lower 2027 marketing. That points to a cut or a low-end/trim. Offsets: NA marketing +63% in Q2, $6.5m of H2 cost savings, and DraftKings' heavy Q3 acquisition spend.

evidence.text: The FY26 guide ($45-50m adj EBITDA, $165-170m revenue) needs H2 adj EBITDA of $28.3-33.3m, i.e. about $14-17m a quarter, against Q2's $7.7m and Q1's $9.0m. H2 revenue must be $86.8-91.8m (+2% to +7.5% YoY vs H2 2025's $85.4m) after Q2 printed -5% YoY. Street FY revenue sits at $165.4m, the bottom of the range, so the street already leans to the low end.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name trades on the FY guide: cut on 2025-11-13 -27%, cut on 2026-05-14 -38%, reiterated on 2026-08-13 +19%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The -59% since the last print and an EV of about 3x guided EBITDA show the market has already discounted a cut, while the published consensus and the $4.43 targets still sit on the guide. What is not priced is the size: if the cut takes EBITDA to the high $30m's, covenant headroom (see the covenant finding) becomes the issue, not the cut itself.
evidence.independence: Q1 figures come from a different document (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260514278394/en, Q1 adj EBITDA $9.0m). On the Q2 call (https://www.webull.ca/news-detail/15401380805108736) the CFO said 'what would really push us towards the top of the range would be a recovery in SEO', and an analyst noted the midpoint implies about 5% H2 growth. Shares a document with the covenant finding and the Q3 revenue inference.

evidence.text: Catena Media, a US-focused SEO/CPA casino and sports affiliate (97% of revenue from North America), pre-announced on 2026-10-19 Q3 2026 revenue -29% to EUR 8.3m and adj EBITDA -75% to EUR 0.7m. It blamed AI-driven search changes and lower operator marketing spend, and dropped its 2026 growth target. The final report on 2026-11-10 showed NA revenue -29% to EUR 7.9m.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Search-driven marketing misses led to the guide cuts: Nov 2025 (spam sites in search, -27%) and May 2026 (weak organic search, -38%).
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced. GRSD fell about 25% in the month after (to $1.17 on 2026-10-26) and on down to $0.74. GRSD's NA marketing grew +63% YoY in Q2 on partner and paid channels, so the transmission is partial and the market may not separate the two.
evidence.independence: Catena's own interim report release, 2026-11-10 (https://www.inderes.se/en/releases/a-disappointing-quarter-as-search-pressures-weigh-on-revenue). Better Collective (separate finding) points the other way for NA.
evidence.link: Same business model and channel as GRSD's marketing segment: organic-search affiliate sites earning CPA from US online casino and sportsbook operators. GRSD marketing was $26.5m of $37.8m Q2 revenue (70%), and its declines came from 'organic search and markets outside North America'. Not a counterparty.

evidence.text: Better Collective Q3 2026 (out 2026-11-18/19): North America revenue +28% to EUR 26.6m with a 39% EBITDA margin, group revenue +6% organic to EUR 83.1m, and FY26 guidance maintained. Low sports win margin cut EUR 6.5m from revenue and EBITDA, and Publishing grew +16%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No GRSD reaction to peer prints has been measured.
evidence.why_not_priced: Published a day before GRSD's print and a European listing, so little time to transmit. The low sports margin is a negative for any revenue-share part of GRSD's book, so the net effect is small.
evidence.independence: Investing.com Q3 slides coverage (https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/better-collective-q3-2026-slides-record-revenue-amid-brazil-crisis-93CH-5038246).
evidence.link: Affiliate and sports media business paid by the same US operators. BC's NA growth credited revenue-share, prediction markets and talent-led media, which are less SEO-driven than GRSD's model. The share of overlapping clients is not stated.

evidence.text: Covenant and obligations: the Wells Fargo facility caps leverage at 3.00x, with a fixed-charge minimum of 1.25x and a $15.0m minimum liquidity. Borrowings were $122.3m at 30 June against cash of $8.8m and total liquidity of $33.3m, with net current liabilities of $23.1m. A further $26.5m of OddsJam deferred consideration is now current (due about April 2027, up to 70% settleable in shares), plus Spotlight.Vegas earnouts of up to $11m in April 2027. LTM adj EBITDA is about $45.1m (Q3'25 $13.0m + Q4'25 about $15.4m + Q1'26 $9.0m + Q2'26 $7.7m), so gross leverage is about 2.7x. If Q3'26 EBITDA comes in below about $9.6m in place of Q3'25's $13.0m, gross leverage passes 3.0x unless covenant EBITDA adds back restructuring.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for this line. The company has had no covenant event or equity raise since its IPO.
evidence.why_not_priced: Asked what the money buys: it pays for past acquisitions (OddsJam, Spotlight), not a visible ramp, so the sign is negative. A $26m market cap against $122m of debt says equity holders already fear dilution. What is not priced is the specific trigger: a share-settled earnout at $0.74 (about $18.5m / $0.74 = about 25m shares against 35.6m outstanding) or a covenant amendment announced with the print. A clean statement of headroom would relieve that fear, hence the positive high end.
evidence.independence: Covenant terms are in the Q1 2026 6-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001839799/000183979926000101/q12026quarterlyfinancials.htm). The leverage path is my own arithmetic, an inference. The FY25 Q4 EBITDA is derived from the FY25 total of $58.0m in the 20-F.

evidence.why_not_priced: The de-rating is itself the price; the finding is that the bar a beat must clear is lower than three months ago. If the market were pricing a clean beat and guide, the stock would not be at its lows into the print with downside skew bid.

evidence.why_not_priced: The release says the quarter closed Oct 31 with demand strong and no change to the guide, which rules out a miss on demand; the market sold the stock through it anyway, so the 'no miss' content is not reflected in a price that fell further after it. The departing CFO giving his last guide is a small risk of a conservative Q1 frame.
evidence.independence: Sept 11 Goldman remarks also reiterated the $1.94bn Q4 midpoint (https://quartr.com/events/keysight-technologies-inc-keys-goldman-sachs-communacopia-technology-conference-2026_3gx1pBHu).

evidence.text: At Goldman Sachs Communacopia (2026-09-11) management said about $100M of orders had slipped beyond the normal shipment window on component bottlenecks, reiterated Q4 at $1.94bn, and said revenue should exceed $2bn a quarter once constraints ease; with orders above $2bn for three straight quarters and book-to-bill above 1.1, a Q1 FY27 guide at or above $2bn is possible if supply loosens, against street ~$1.95-1.96bn.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide above street bought +10.0% (Nov 2025) and +23.1% (Feb 2026); a guide above street with a supply warning sold -6.3% (Aug 2026) (baseline; https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/22/why-keysight-technologies-stock-sank-this-week/).
evidence.why_not_priced: The stock fell 5.2% on 2026-09-14 on this supply talk (https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Keysight+Technologies+Slides+as+AI+Hardware+Weakness+and+Supply-Constraint+Talk+Weigh+on+Shares), so the market read the slip as a negative while the same remark sizes deferred revenue that lands in later quarters; a Q1 guide of ~$1.95bn street does not reflect a backlog release. Sized small because the CFO said on Aug 18 the constraint would limit conversion for about two quarters, i.e. through Q1.
evidence.independence: CFO on 2026-08-18: 'demand is not the limiter', supply 'likely to be nonlinear' for about two quarters (https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262116238-tradingkey); Ralliant flagged 'constrained supply' on 2026-11-04, so the component squeeze persisted into the quarter.

evidence.text: The CFO said on the Q3 call that one-time tariff impacts 'artificially pulled up '26 profitability that won't repeat', so the FY27 frame and the Q1 EPS guide start from a base that includes a non-recurring benefit; the leverage target (>40% incrementals) is stated ex one-time items, which leaves room for a Q1 EPS guide below what a naive extrapolation of Q4's ~$3.37 implies.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Aug 2026 print sold -6.3% / -11.7% on the week when management flagged softer FY27 growth/margin risk (https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/22/why-keysight-technologies-stock-sank-this-week/).
evidence.why_not_priced: It is public but the FY27 EPS consensus is stale and scattered ($8.77 to ~$10.97 across pages), so it is unclear the street netted the tariff item out; if it had, the Q1 EPS consensus would sit visibly below Q4's level. Sized small because management also says gross margin in the upper 60s is sustainable and synergies add ~$50M into FY27.
evidence.independence: Earnings Whispers preview (2026-11-11) names the non-recurring tariff benefit as a key test; Ralliant and Viavi both carried IEEPA tariff refunds in their September quarters (https://finviz.com/news/415674/ralliant-beats-and-raises-again-as-growth-accelerates-to-17-but-tariff-refunds-and-inventory-build-temper-the-margin-story).

evidence.text: On 2026-09-01 (8-K filed 09-04) Matthews signed a Ninth Amendment to its credit agreement. It excludes the Propelis 40% stake from the leverage ratio, cuts the revolver from $700M to $650M and removes the $350M foreign borrowing facility. What the money buys: covenant headroom, not a ramp. Net debt was $529.7M at Q3 against an ex-Propelis EBITDA run rate of roughly $115-120M, so about 4.5x against a 2.5x target.

evidence.text: Street FY27 adjusted EPS is $12.24, only +4% on FY26 consensus of $11.77 (stockanalysis), but FY26 adjusted includes about $0.70 from the $30M IEEPA tariff refund that management called largely non-recurring. Ex-refund, the street needs about +12% from a clean base of about $11.0. Moog's last first guide (FY26: $10.00 vs FY25 $8.69, +15%) cleared a similar bar, its twelve-month backlog was +23% at June (vs street FY27 revenue +7.3%), and the CEO said on 31 Jul he was 'pretty confident' on FY27. Net: an initiation at or above $12.24 is more likely than not. The risk is a headline that management frames off the refund-inflated $11.65+ base, which the Earnings Whispers preview names as the outcome that 'would confirm market doubts'.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: First guide on 2025-11-21 (FY26 at $10.00, read as above consensus): +8.16%. The raise on 2026-07-31, where the raise was mostly refund, was sold -7.01%. Raises on 2026-01-30 and 2026-04-24 were bought +6.02% and +2.26% (baseline history).
evidence.why_not_priced: The stock is 24-25% below the lowest sell-side target and -13.7% since the Q3 print, while FY27 consensus still sits at $12.24 (targets last moved in October). If the market believed in a clean +12% FY27, the stock would not trade at the low end of its 52-week range on a de-rated multiple. The drawdown says the market doubts the street number. The open question is whether management's first number validates it, and that is unpriced by construction until the release.
evidence.independence: Q3 call transcript (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2943055, 2026-07-31) for 'pretty confident' and missile upside not in backlog. Q3 8-K exhibit for the $30M refund at 270 bp and the twelve-month backlog of $3.3B (+23%) (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000067887/000162828026051250/ex991-73126.htm). evidence.text: Lockheed Martin booked the PAC-3 MSE multiyear into backlog in Q3 (record $292.0B backlog including $52.5B for the PAC-3 MSE multiyear; reported 2026-10-22) and raised its 2026 guide on PAC-3/THAAD/GMLRS output. On 31 Jul Moog's CEO said 'there is significant more upside to come on the missiles that is not yet reflected in our business backlog', with PAC-3 production step-ups of about 3x. Moog's Q4 (Sep quarter) backlog and FY27 Space & Defense guide are the first place the sub-tier award can show.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Backlog has been a driver: the record $3B backlog in Nov 2025 accompanied +8.16%. The deceleration of twelve-month backlog growth to 23% from 33% at Q3 is cited as part of the -7.01% reaction.
evidence.why_not_priced: Moog has not spoken since 31 Jul. The preview (2026-11-15) still describes Lockheed's framework agreements as 'not yet in backlog' for Moog. If the market expected a backlog step-up, the post-Q3 backlog-deceleration narrative would have faded and the stock would not have fallen 13.7% since.
evidence.independence: Moog Q3 call (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2943055) is a different document from Lockheed's release. The timing of Moog's sub-award booking is an inference: Moog has not confirmed it.
evidence.link: Moog supplies the custom actuators for Lockheed's PAC-3 MSE interceptor, described as one of the largest awards in Moog Defense's history (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250129830001/en). Moog guided FY26 missile revenue to about $275M, roughly 6% of $4.4B sales.

evidence.text: Two of Moog's largest commercial programs are stalled at the OEM. Boeing said on 2026-10-27 that the 787 is holding at 8/month (not the planned 10) on engine and delivery issues. Airbus's CEO said on 2026-10-28 that the A350 had run 'below rate four' for some months or quarters, with only 38 A350 deliveries in 9M26 and three in September. Both points came after Moog's 31 Jul call, where the CEO said 787/A350 production plans were 'pretty consistent' with customer needs. They lean the FY27 Commercial Aircraft OEM guide cautious. Commercial Aircraft was $253.6M of $1,116.5M in Q3 (23%), with OEM only part of it, and the rest of the company (defense, industrial at +17-18%) must carry growth.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FY26 outlook was already trimmed for commercial aircraft inventory timing (preview). No clean reaction to that line alone is visible in the baseline.
evidence.why_not_priced: Both counterparty statements came after Moog's last call, and Moog's FY27 commercial guide has not been set against them. But they were public weeks ago and the whole aerospace group traded on them, so this is a proxy that is partly priced. If the market had fully priced it, sell-side FY27 revenue (+7.3%) would have come down; targets last moved on 2026-10-13, before both releases.
evidence.independence: Boeing Q3 release: https://boeing.mediaroom.com/2026-10-27-Boeing-Reports-Third-Quarter-Results (different document, same direction). Moog has not confirmed any impact; this is a transmission inference.
evidence.link: Moog makes flight-control actuation for the Boeing 787 and high-lift actuation for the A350. On the Q3 call the analyst question on A350/787 sell-in vs assembly rates shows these are the programs the line turns on (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2943055). Commercial Aircraft is 23% of Q3 sales.

evidence.text: MV75 (Bell/Textron) funding gap closed: Congress approved a $350M Army reprogramming for FY26 MV75 funding, and about $300M was obligated during Textron's Q3 to cover costs already incurred by Textron and its suppliers. Textron had been self-funding since July. On 31 Jul Moog said some program spend was capped by a do-not-exceed limit already in its guidance, and the Earnings Whispers preview flagged 'limited visibility into early calendar 2027'.

evidence.why_not_priced: The 15 Nov preview still lists MV75 visibility as a risk, so the resolution has not reached the Moog narrative. evidence.text: Q4 is pinned by the company's own narrowed FY26 guide: $1,560-1,570m less 9M adj EBITDA of $1,190.5m implies Q4 $369.5-379.5m (-11 to -13% vs Q4 FY25's ~$425m). evidence.why_not_priced: It is priced: a guide range only $10m wide one quarter out leaves little room. It is filed so the judges see that the quarter cannot carry the move; a $10m beat is about 0.6% of annual EBITDA.
evidence.independence: Q1/Q2 adj EBITDA ($418.2m, $395.0m) from the Q1 and Q2 8-Ks (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1530950/000153095026000019/ex99-1q12026er.htm) confirm the 9M sum. Same company documents.

evidence.text: Shell egg prices collapsed during Post's Q4 (Jul-Sep): Cal-Maine's quarter to 2026-08-29 showed conventional egg ASP -59.3% and a $58.6m net loss, and it expects continued pressure. That speeds the fade of the ~$60m foodservice earnings above the $500m run rate and is the input to FY27 foodservice. It also eases the 'market-priced vs grain-based egg cost' gap that hurt Refrigerated Retail in Q3. Fall HPAI outbreaks (IL 0.93m birds on 10-19, CA 1.3m on 10-28, about 0.5% of the flock) are too small to reverse it.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Foodservice upside drove the Q1 FY26 raise (+9.77%, 2026-02-05); its 'normalisation' framing accompanied the -12.79% Q3 reaction.
evidence.why_not_priced: Management already guides foodservice to a $500m run rate, so the direction is known. Not known is whether a deeper-than-modelled egg collapse puts FY27 foodservice below $500m. If the market had priced that, previews would cite a foodservice cut; the EW preview still frames a 'gentle landing'. The net is small because Refrigerated Retail gains on the cost side.
evidence.independence: Fall HPAI outbreak sizes from Food Ingredients First (https://www.foodingredientsfirst.com/news/bird-flu-egg-chicken-prices), a different source. It cuts slightly the other way, toward firmer prices into FY27 Q1.
evidence.link: Same product and market: Post's Michael Foods (Foodservice, ~$140m Q3 EBITDA, about 37% of company EBITDA) sells egg products partly at market-indexed prices and buys outside eggs. Cal-Maine is the largest US shell-egg producer and its ASP is the market series.

evidence.text: The formal FY27 guide is the swing factor and leans down. On the Q3 call (2026-08-07), management said inflation was tracking toward the high end of expectations, offsetting pricing was weighted to the back half of FY27, and the budget was 'under development'. A new CEO (Catoggio, from 2026-10-01) gives his first guide, and the preliminary view was 'generally flat' vs ~$1.48bn. A range centered below $1.48bn is the main downside; a reaffirmed $1.48bn midpoint is the upside case.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide line moves this stock: the first FY26 guide (2025-11-20) -7.15%, the Q1 FY26 raise +9.77%, the preliminary FY27 flat/rebase -12.79%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is near its lows and targets are being cut (Barclays $88 on 11-19). But the August rebase was framed as the final reset and the preview's central case is a reaffirmed flat. A guide centered below $1.48bn is not the modelled case. If it were priced, estimate revisions would show FY27 EBITDA below $1.48bn, and none was found.
evidence.independence: Q3 release text: 'budget remains under development'; Foodservice growth, pricing and productivity to offset inflation and volume softness (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001530950/000153095026000076/ex99-1q32026er.htm). A market braced for good news would show a run-up into the print; this one shows a run-down.

evidence.text: The consensus bar for consolidated profit is high against Q2. MarketScreener has Q3 net income RMB304m, EBIT RMB213m and EPS RMB0.25; Chartmill has EPS RMB0.23. evidence.why_not_priced: Two to six analysts cover the stock and Chartmill shows revenue estimates revised up 8.55% in three months, which suggests the consolidation is modelled generously. evidence.text: Placer.ai measured Ross same-store visits up 12.3% YoY in Q3 2026, with gains near or above 10% in every month through October. Ross guided a 6-7% comp and consensus is 6.9%. In Q2, total visits up 16.4% went with a 10% comp, so the traffic points to a Q3 comp of roughly 8-10%, above guide and consensus but at or near the buy-side's ~10%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Comp beats have been bought: +8.41% on a 7% comp against a 2-3% guide (2025-11-20), +8.11% (2026-05-21, 17% comp), +4.39% (2026-08-20, 10% comp).
evidence.why_not_priced: The data is public (3 days old) and UBS's ~10% comp call matches it, so it is partly in the whisper. But the stock fell 5.8% in the 5 days into the print and is 18% below the consensus target. If the market fully believed a ~10% comp, the stock would not have lagged XRT by 3.6 pts this week.
evidence.independence: UBS's independent ~10% comp estimate (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/ross-stores-earnings-in-focus-can-momentum-sustain-after-q2-beat-93CH-5039346). Management said on 2026-08-20 that August was 'encouraging' (separate finding). Proxy: visits are not sales, and the Q2 visits-to-comp gap was about 6 pts.

evidence.text: The real bar is above consensus. The Earnings Whispers whisper is $1.91 against $1.82 consensus and a $1.83 guide top; consensus has risen from $1.74. UBS says investors expect a ~10% comp, 11c-beat type of report. A print that only beats the 6.9% / $1.82 consensus can disappoint.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's EPS beat (~$2.06 ex-refund against a $1.94 consensus, ~6%) bought only +4.39%, the weakest of the last four positive reactions.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus figures sit at $1.82-1.86 and are what wire headlines will compare against. The buy-side bar is not in the published consensus, so a 'beat' headline can still fall short of what holders want.
evidence.independence: UBS investor-conversations comment (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/ross-stores-earnings-in-focus-can-momentum-sustain-after-q2-beat-93CH-5039346, 2026-11-19); independent of Earnings Whispers.

evidence.why_not_priced: This is a price fact, so it is priced by definition. What it changes is the bar: a name that ran into the print would need more. If holders were still positioned for a blowout, ROST would have tracked TJX's +8% on 11-18 rather than lagging by 4.7 pts.
evidence.independence: XRT, TJX and BURL charts (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/XRT?range=1mo&interval=1d, https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/TJX?range=1mo&interval=1d, https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/BURL?range=1mo&interval=1d). evidence.text: TJX reported the same quarter (Aug-Oct) on 2026-11-18. Consolidated comp was +4% against a +2-3% plan, Marmaxx +2% (from +1% in Q2) with flat transactions, and the back half of the quarter was stronger. Merchandise availability was 'outstanding' and closeouts were increasing. No shift by income group. TJX rose +8.0%. The off-price channel was healthy and better-than-plan comps were rewarded.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: ROST gained +3.3% on TJX's print day, about 40% of TJX's own move.
evidence.why_not_priced: ROST has partly absorbed it (+3.3% on 11-18), then gave back 1.6% on 11-19. The read-through to Ross's own comp is still unproven. Marmaxx improving is also a competitive point, since Placer shows T.J. Maxx visits turned positive in September and accelerated in October.
evidence.independence: TJX call transcript (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/11/18/tjx-tjx-q3-2027-earnings-call-transcript/) and longbridge on the +11% intraday move (https://longbridge.com/en/news/306008293). Same event.
evidence.link: Direct competitor in the same channel: Marmaxx (T.J. Maxx/Marshalls) is the closest US analogue to Ross, with the same off-price apparel/home model, the same branded-closeout vendor pool and an overlapping value shopper. TJX's quarter ended 2026-11-01, Ross's 2026-10-31.

evidence.text: Next-guide risk: TJX cut its Q4 margin and EPS outlook (adj EPS $1.42-1.45 against a $1.49 street) explicitly for higher fuel, called fuel/freight 'the largest headwind', and said unseasonably warm US weather was holding back demand in early Q4. Ross does not hedge fuel, its guide 'includes current higher fuel prices' as of August, and its Q4 compares against a +9% comp. This makes a Q4 raise unlikely; a maintain is the base case.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Nov 2025 Ross raised its Q4 comp guide to +3-4% and rose +8.41%. In May 2025 it pulled its annual forecast and fell -9.85%. The guide has driven the largest moves.
evidence.why_not_priced: The market rewarded TJX's comps and looked through its Q4 fuel cut (+8%). Investing.com's preview expects Ross to maintain Q4, so a maintain is roughly the base case. The risk is a Q4 EPS guide below the street if Ross also lowers margin for fuel. Diesel has eased to $5.94 (11-16) from the $6.35 Oct peak, which softens this.
evidence.independence: Ross's own Q2-call fuel language (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-ross-stores-tops-q2-2026-estimates-shares-jump-after-hours-93CH-4870582). Shares the fuel series with the diesel finding below, which lands on the Q3 margin rather than the guide.
evidence.link: Same channel and same freight/fuel exposure. Ross's CFO said fuel is the largest part of freight and is unhedged (Q2 call). Same holiday quarter and weather exposure.

evidence.text: Diesel rose after Ross set its Q3 guide on 2026-08-20. The EIA average was $5.454 the week of Aug 17 and peaked at $6.352 on Oct 26 (now $5.937). Ross's Q3 EBIT margin guide of 11.7-12.0% already assumed fuel-related freight pressure at August prices, and fuel cost 10bp in Q2. The extra cost is perhaps 5-15bp of Q3 margin, roughly $0.01-0.03 of EPS.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior ROST print turned on freight; Q2's 10bp fuel hit was swamped by a 205bp ex-refund margin gain.
evidence.why_not_priced: Small enough to be covered by comp leverage. TJX's Marmaxx margin fell 110bp, mainly on freight/fuel, so if the market extrapolates that, Ross's margin beat could look lower quality than its sales beat.
evidence.independence: FRED/EIA August series (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/?g=1XTvU) and FleetOwner 2026-11-11 (https://www.fleetowner.com/emissions-efficiency/news/55417900/us-diesel-prices-fall-nationwide-as-trucking-fuel-costs-remain-37-higher-year-over-year). This is macro-to-company transmission; Ross confirmed it is unhedged but did not give a sensitivity.

evidence.text: Ross's reaction function pays for beats. 6 of the last 7 prints were up, with a median absolute move of 8.03%; Q3 last year (+7% comp against a 2-3% guide, Q4 raised) bought +8.41%. Ross has raised its outlook on each of the last three calls. The most recent, largest beat (Q2) bought only +4.39%, so the payoff per point of beat is shrinking.
evidence.why_not_priced: A base rate, partly priced through the call-side skew. Reported here so the judges can weigh the name's pattern of buying beat-and-raise prints against the shrinking Q2 response.
evidence.independence: The baseline's 8-K-timed reaction history (sealed file); Investing.com on the Q2 37% beat.

evidence.why_not_priced: Burlington's price reinvestment is known but its effect on Ross's margin has not been measured. Placer's +12.3% Ross traffic argues it has not cost Ross volume.
evidence.independence: TJX call, on lowering prices where competitors cut (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/11/18/tjx-tjx-q3-2027-earnings-call-transcript/).
evidence.link: Burlington is the third national off-price chain, with the same low/middle-income value shopper and overlapping store footprint. Ross's dd's and Ross banners compete most directly with Burlington on price point.

evidence.text: TJX booked another $132M of IEEPA tariff refunds in its Q3. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's refund (+$0.60 EPS) came with a +4.39% reaction; holders appeared to look through it to the ex-refund beat.
evidence.why_not_priced: Speculative and below the line; it would distort the headline EPS comparison against $1.82 but has no path to the guide.
evidence.independence: TJX Q3 refund disclosure (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000109198/000010919826000058/tjxq3fy27earningspressrele.htm).

session_conflict.note: the event date carries the volume spike, so the market reacted on that date and the print was bmo. If tagged amc, the recorded move is the day-after give-back and may carry the wrong sign.

history.basis: 6-K exhibit text matched results language (8 filings opened). Heuristic, not an item code: a 6-K carrying results language is very likely an earnings release but this is weaker than the 8-K item 2.02 path

event_plausibility.reason: inferred cadence of 10 days is too short to be an earnings cadence (quarterly is ~91, semi-annual ~182), so the 8 matched filings are not earnings -- most likely monthly operational updates caught by the 6-K text matcher. No cadence verdict is possible and the reaction history above should not be used as an earnings base rate. Confirm the date from a company source instead.

options.skew_note: IV(25d put) - IV(25d call). Positive = the market is paying more for downside protection than for upside.

baseline.deadband_basis: half the median of 8 prior reactions, floored at 1.5%
baseline.deadband_note: A realised move inside this band is scored as no-direction rather than as a miss.
baseline.expected_move_basis: median historical reaction (no usable option chain)

baseline_quality.note: thin means there is no reliable statement of what the market priced, so a confident call on this name cannot be justified by the baseline.

evidence.text: The robotaxi fleet did not grow during Q3. The Q2 release counted 'more than 1,800 robotaxis' (about 3,400 AVs) as of 31 Jul 2026, and the 27 Oct 2026 insurance-program release still says 'more than 1,800 Robotaxis' (about 3,600 AVs). Reaching the 2,600 end-2026 target therefore needs about +800 robotaxis in roughly two months. Pony, by contrast, had 2,768 at 30 Sep and kept its 3,500 target.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Fleet targets are the stock's narrative anchor. The Q2 print (fleet +500 q/q, overseas fleet doubled) still fell 9.7%, so fleet growth alone has not lifted the stock, but a stall or a cut has not yet been tested.
evidence.why_not_priced: The fleet figure sat in an insurance-program press release, not a results release, and no preview found compares it with the 31 Jul count. Earnings Whispers on 15 Nov still describes the 2,600 target as 'unchanged'. If the market had priced the stall, previews would be asking whether the target holds. Part of the 25% week may be this, but the drawdown tracked Pony's day by day, which points to a sector move rather than a company one.
evidence.independence: The Q2 6-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001867729/000110465926094571/tm2622690d2_ex99-1.htm, 12 Aug 2026) gives the 31 Jul baseline of more than 1,800 robotaxis. The target and its 'subject to conditions' caveat are in the 23 Mar 2026 release. The Geely Farizon GXR upgrade rolling off production in Q3 2026 (https://finviz.com/news/333226/weride-and-geely-farizon-to-deliver-2000-purpose-built-robotaxi-gxrs-by-2026-advancing-large-scale-global-commercialization) is the path by which the stall could reverse in Q4. 'More than 1,800' is a floor, so the true October count could be somewhat higher.

evidence.text: Peer read-through. Pony AI reported Q3 2026 on 18 Nov before the open: revenue of US$44.6M (+75% y/y) against Benzinga's pre-report estimate of $39.1M, robotaxi revenue +165%, gross margin down to 17.8%, and the 3,500-vehicle and 3.5x robotaxi revenue targets reaffirmed. PONY fell 7.3% that day (3.99 to 3.70 on 11.9M shares, about 4x average) and about 4.7% more on 19 Nov. The market sold a beat-and-reaffirm in the same business, the same quarter, two days before WRD reports.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: WRD moved -7.1% on Pony's results day, on 2.4x its normal volume, so this peer's prints transmit directly. In April 2025 the two moved in opposite directions on a Pony product event.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: WRD has already fallen about 17% since Pony reported. What is not settled is the reaction function, that a sector beat with reaffirmed targets was sold, which applies to WRD's own release tomorrow. Had WRD fully discounted it, there would be no further drift into the print, yet it was still falling about 10% intraday on 19 Nov.
evidence.independence: Prices are from https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/PONY?range=1mo&interval=1d. The Pony estimate is from Benzinga (https://benzinga.com/z/49055208, snippet only). This shares the Yahoo tape with the expectations finding below, but reads a different object (the peer's reaction to a beat versus WRD's own drawdown).

evidence.text: Customer volume supports the ADAS line. GAC Aion N60, the first mass-production car with WeRide's WRD 3.0 one-stage ADAS, passed 20,000 users in under five months, and Aion i60 orders passed 20,000 by end-September (the i60 runs on WRD 3.0 per WeRide's 15 Sep 2026 release). GAC Hyper/Aion BU sold 35,494 units in September, +21.9% y/y. Q2 L2++/L3 deliveries were about 30,000 units, worth roughly RMB 106M (total revenue less L4).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The ADAS ramp drove Q2's +103% q/q revenue jump. That beat was sold (-9.7%) because the loss did not narrow, so the line has paid on the number but not on the stock.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus of RMB 270M implies only +16.5% q/q after a +103% quarter. If the ADAS run-rate held at or above 30k units with N60/i60 volumes, the street would be nearer the top of its range (RMB 305M) than the middle. The September sales data comes from Chinese auto press that ADR previews do not cite.

Customer user counts are cumulative marketing figures, not monthly deliveries.
evidence.link: GAC Aion is a WRD 3.0 customer. The N60 and i60 are named WRD 3.0 programs. Per-unit ADAS revenue is roughly RMB 3,500 (Q2 non-L4 revenue of about RMB 106M over about 30k units), and ADAS was about 46% of Q2 revenue.

evidence.text: Q3 revenue is likely to clear the RMB 270M bar. It needs only +16.5% q/q on Q2's RMB 231.7M, which itself followed Q1's 114.1M. Q4 seasonality (Q4 2025 was 314M, with heavy product sales) means the street has back-loaded the year (Q4 consensus 514M). But this name sold its last beat (Q2 revenue beat, -9.7%).

evidence.text: The buyback is largely spent and paused. The HKEX monthly return for October 2026 shows 40,454,099 Class A shares in treasury and issued shares unchanged in the month, against 25.16M treasury shares on 13 May 2026. At the roughly $2.2-2.5 per-share prices of the May-June buying, 40.45M shares is about $90-100M, close to the $100M program approved in March 2026, which runs until March 2027. A re-authorisation at the print is possible. The last buyback announcement (with Q4 2025) coincided with +9%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: 23 Mar 2026: Q4 results plus a $100M buyback, +9% (https://www.stocktitan.net/news/WRD/we-ride-reports-record-full-year-2025-revenue-of-rmb684-6-million-up-jk4jsjcttsk5.html).
evidence.why_not_priced: Treasury accounting is in an HKEX form, not a wire story, and no preview mentions that the program is near exhaustion. Sign is ambiguous: losing the support bid is negative, while a re-up at a 52-week low with about $790M of cash would be positive. Net sized small and positive with a wide band.
evidence.independence: May treasury count and buy prices: https://www.itiger.com/news/1102482285 (14 May 2026). Treasury shares may not all come from this program, so the dollar estimate is an inference.
